fact.claim: Cipher Mining (CIFR) hit its all-time low of US$0.38 on December 29, 2022, and its all-time high of US$30.14 on June 22, 2026. TradingView does not say whether the $0.38 low is a closing price or an intraday price. On November 5, 2026 the stock was around US$5.11, down about 20% in one day, so $1,000 put in at the 2022 low would be worth roughly $13,400 today, but only someone who bought on that exact day would have got that. CIFR is below its late-2021 level of about US$7.89, so the gain only shows up when you measure from the 2022 low, not over the full 5 years.

plain.what: Cipher Mining, called CIFR on the stock market, is a company whose computers make new bitcoin. It now also rents out giant buildings full of computers that run AI, and Amazon signed a 15-year rent deal with it worth about $5.5 billion. On December 29, 2022 its share price fell to US$0.38, the lowest it has ever been, and on November 5, 2026 it dropped about 20% in one day to around US$5.11.
plain.so_what: Someone who put in $1,000 at US$7.89 and sold on that worst day walked away with $48, while the same shares held would be worth about $648 today.
plain.do: Write down the price you paid for anything you own, so you can do the math yourself on the next scary day.
